chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and did not enter (consume the marriage) with her. He (peace be upon him) said: If she dies, or he dies, or he divorces her, then for her is half (the dower), and upon her is the complete waiting period, and for her is the inheritance.

key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: Waiting period (iddah) observed after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a wife who is divorced or widowed before consummation of marriage in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this foundational narration from al-Kafi, Ubayd ibn Zurara queries Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the status of a woman married but not yet consummated with, establishing the triad of rights: half the dower, full iddah, and inheritance. This ruling serves as the primary evidence in Shia jurisprudence for the 'half-dower' principle, distinguishing it from the full dower granted upon consummation, and underscores the legal reality of the marital bond even before physical union.
